# Oslo Hiking Tours

> Private guided day trips from Oslo to Norway's greatest mountains. Hotel pickup included. Up to 4 guests per trip.
>
> Season status: winter tours in Nordmarka (Winter Forest Hike, Campfire Evening Walk) are open for bookings, December 2026 to March 2027. The Oslo Coffee Walk, a specialty coffee walking tour in the city centre, runs all year. Summer day trips and the overnight reopen for summer 2027; enquiries for 2027 dates are welcome now.

Oslo Hiking Tours is a private guided hiking company based in Oslo, Norway. In summer we offer day trips from Oslo to Norway's most iconic mountain destinations — Gaustatoppen and Vettakollen; in winter, easy guided outings in Nordmarka, Oslo's forest. Summer day trips include a private guide, hotel pickup in Oslo, and all driving to and from the trailhead. Guests simply show up — we handle everything else.

## Winter Tours (December–March)

Both winter tours are private (up to 4 guests), meet in central Oslo and travel to Nordmarka by metro. Metro tickets and food are not included. Guests bring warm winter boots.

### Winter Forest Hike
- Difficulty: Easy
- Duration: About 4 hours, including the metro
- Price: NOK 4,000 per group (up to 4 guests)
- Description: A guided winter hike in Nordmarka, the forest on Oslo's doorstep. Snowshoes when there is snow, ice spikes and poles when it is icy — the tour runs in all winter conditions. Starts around 10:00.
- URL: https://www.oslohikingtours.no/winter-forest-hike

### Campfire Evening Walk
- Difficulty: Easy
- Duration: About 3 hours, including the metro
- Price: NOK 3,500 per group (up to 4 guests)
- Description: A guided evening walk by headlamp through Nordmarka's winter forest to a campfire lit by the guide. Starts around 16:00, after dark. Headlamps provided; ice spikes when icy.
- URL: https://www.oslohikingtours.no/campfire-evening-walk

## Walking Tours

Oslo Hiking Tours runs private walking tours in Oslo — just your group and a local guide, never strangers. Overview: https://www.oslohikingtours.no/walking-tours-oslo
- Oslo Coffee Walk (city, year-round, about 3 hours, NOK 3,000 per group, coffee not included)
- Campfire Evening Walk (Nordmarka forest by headlamp, December–March, about 3 hours, NOK 3,500 per group)
- Winter Forest Hike (Nordmarka, snowshoes or ice spikes, December–March, about 4 hours, NOK 4,000 per group)

## City Tour (year-round)

### Oslo Coffee Walk
- Difficulty: Easy
- Duration: About 3 hours, about 4 km on foot
- Price: NOK 3,000 per group (up to 4 guests); coffee and food not included (guests pay at each café)
- Description: A private guided walking tour of Oslo's specialty coffee scene. Four stops — Fuglen (city centre), Java (St. Hanshaugen), Supreme Roastworks (Vulkan, by the Akerselva river) and Tim Wendelboe (Grünerløkka, World Barista Champion 2004) — walking from the city centre via St. Hanshaugen park and the Akerselva river path to Grünerløkka. A bike version (22 km) is offered by sister company Oslo Bike Tours: https://www.oslobiketours.no/oslo-coffee-tour/
- URL: https://www.oslohikingtours.no/oslo-coffee-walk

## Our Tours

### Vettakollen Viewpoint
- Difficulty: Easy
- Duration: 3.5 hours hiking
- Drive from Oslo: 30 minutes
- Price: NOK 4,000 per group (up to 4 guests)
- Description: A guided hike to the Vettakollen viewpoint in Nordmarka, with sweeping panoramic views over Oslo and the Oslofjord. Ideal for families and first-time visitors.
- URL: https://www.oslohikingtours.no/vettakollen-summit

### Gaustatoppen
- Difficulty: Moderate
- Duration: 4–5 hours hiking
- Drive from Oslo: 2.5 hours
- Price: NOK 10,000 per group (up to 4 guests)
- Description: A guided day trip to Gaustatoppen (1,883m) in Telemark — Norway's most spectacular viewpoint. On a clear day you can see one sixth of Norway from the summit.
- URL: https://www.oslohikingtours.no/gaustatoppen

## Experiences

### Overnight in Nordmarka
- Type: Overnight forest camping experience (not a day trip)
- Duration: Afternoon to the following morning (roughly 18 hours)
- Drive from Oslo: 30–45 minutes
- Price: NOK 12,000 per group (up to 4 guests)
- Description: A private guided overnight camping experience in Nordmarka, the forest wilderness on Oslo's doorstep. Guests hike in to a secluded spot in the late afternoon, the guide cooks dinner over an open fire at sunset, guests sleep in tents under the stars, and wake to a forest sunrise before hiking back out. All camping equipment (tents, sleeping bags, mats, cooking gear) is provided — nothing to bring.
- URL: https://www.oslohikingtours.no/overnight-nordmarka

## Key Facts

- Winter tours (Winter Forest Hike, Campfire Evening Walk) run December–March and are open for bookings.
- The Oslo Coffee Walk runs all year.
- Summer day trips and the overnight are closed until summer 2027. Guests can already send an enquiry for a 2027 date via the booking form.
- All trips are private — no strangers, just your group and your guide
- Standard trips priced for groups of up to 4 guests; larger groups welcome — contact for a tailored quote
- Summer day trips: hotel pickup in Oslo and all driving included
- Winter tours: meet in central Oslo, travel by metro
- Trips operate as day trips — guests return to Oslo the same day
- Bookings via enquiry form at https://www.oslohikingtours.no/#book
- Contact: post@oslohikingtours.no
- Based in Oslo, Norway

## About

Oslo Hiking Tours was founded to give visitors and locals alike access to Norway's greatest mountain experiences without the complexity of planning, driving and navigating unfamiliar terrain. Our guides are experienced, local and passionate about Norway's mountains.

## Common Questions

**What is Oslo Hiking Tours?**
Oslo Hiking Tours is a private guided hiking company based in Oslo, Norway. We take small groups (up to 4 guests) from Oslo to Norway's most iconic destinations: in winter, snowshoe hikes and campfire evening walks in Nordmarka by metro from central Oslo; in summer, day trips to Gaustatoppen and Vettakollen with hotel pickup. All trips are private (no strangers).

**Is hotel pickup included?**
On summer day trips, yes — pickup from your hotel or accommodation in central Oslo. Winter tours meet in central Oslo and travel to the forest by metro. You do not need a car or any local knowledge — we handle everything.

**What is included in the price?**
The price covers your private guide, hotel pickup in Oslo, all driving to and from the trailhead, and full mountain guidance throughout the day. Food and refreshments at mountain huts or cafés along the way are not included.

**How do I book?**
Send an enquiry through the booking form at oslohikingtours.no or email post@oslohikingtours.no. We will confirm availability and arrange the details directly with you.

**What languages do you guide in?**
We guide in English.

**Are the tours private?**
Yes — every trip is fully private. You will not be grouped with strangers. The trip is just your group and your guide.

**How many people can join a trip?**
Standard trips are priced for groups of up to 4 guests. Larger groups are welcome — contact us for a tailored quote.

**What happens if the weather is bad?**
Your guide monitors conditions in the days before your trip. If conditions are unsafe or unsuitable, we contact you to discuss rescheduling. Safety always comes first.

**Do I need hiking experience?**
It depends on the tour. Vettakollen is suitable for most walkers with basic fitness. Gaustatoppen requires good walking fitness.

**What should I bring?**
Good hiking boots (ankle support is important on the mountain tours), warm layers, a waterproof jacket, sun protection, and enough food and water for a full day. Your guide will give specific packing advice before departure.

**Can children join?**
Older children who can manage a sustained hike are welcome on the Vettakollen tour. For the more challenging tours, contact us to discuss suitability.

**What is the best day trip from Oslo for a first-time visitor?**
Gaustatoppen is a popular choice — a moderately challenging hike with one of the most spectacular summit views in all of Norway, accessible as a comfortable day trip. For something closer to the city, Vettakollen gives a genuine taste of Norwegian forest hiking just 30 minutes from the centre.

**What is the most famous hike in Norway?**
Besseggen Ridge in Jotunheimen is widely considered Norway's most famous mountain hike, attracting around 50,000 hikers per year. Oslo Hiking Tours does not currently offer the Besseggen tour.

**What is the highest mountain in Norway?**
Galdhøpiggen at 2,469m is the highest peak in Norway, in Scandinavia, and in all of Northern Europe. Oslo Hiking Tours does not currently offer guided trips to Galdhøpiggen.

**Is there a private hiking guide available in Oslo?**
Yes — Oslo Hiking Tours offers fully private guided hikes from Oslo to Norway's greatest mountain destinations. In winter, guided snowshoe and campfire walks in Nordmarka; in summer, day trips with hotel pickup and all driving.

**What are the best mountains to visit near Oslo?**
Two classic mountains accessible as day trips from Oslo are Gaustatoppen (Norway's greatest viewpoint, 2.5 hrs) and Vettakollen (Nordmarka forest hike, 30 min from the city).

**How much does a private hiking guide cost in Norway?**
Oslo Hiking Tours charges NOK 3,500 per group for the Campfire Evening Walk and NOK 4,000 for the Winter Forest Hike (winter), NOK 3,000 for the Oslo Coffee Walk (year-round), and NOK 4,000 for Vettakollen and NOK 10,000 for Gaustatoppen (summer). All prices are per group of up to 4 guests — not per person.

**Can I do a Norwegian mountain hike without a car?**
Oslo Hiking Tours is designed precisely for this situation. Summer day trips include hotel pickup in central Oslo and all driving to the trailhead and back. You do not need a car or any knowledge of Norwegian transport to reach any of these destinations with us.

**What can you see from Gaustatoppen?**
On a clear day you can see one sixth of the entire area of Norway from the Gaustatoppen summit — a panorama stretching from the coast to the high mountains in every direction. It is widely considered Norway's most spectacular viewpoint.

**Is Vettakollen suitable for families?**
Yes — Vettakollen is Oslo Hiking Tours' easiest tour. It is a 3.5-hour forest hike with around 380m of elevation gain, on well-marked trails, just 30 minutes from central Oslo. It is suitable for older children and families looking for a genuine taste of Norwegian outdoor life without a long drive.

**What are the best things to do in Oslo in winter?**
Take the metro into Nordmarka, the snowy forest above the city; visit the Holmenkollen ski jump and Ski Museum; sledge the Korketrekkeren toboggan run from Frognerseteren; walk around a frozen Sognsvann; skate at Spikersuppa in the city centre; try a floating fjord sauna; and spend an evening by a campfire in the forest. Oslo Hiking Tours offers a private guided Winter Forest Hike and Campfire Evening Walk. Full guide: https://www.oslohikingtours.no/things-to-do-in-oslo-in-winter

**Can you see the northern lights in Oslo?**
Rarely. Oslo is too far south and too bright for regular northern lights; for reliable sightings, travel to northern Norway.

**What are the best day trips from Oslo?**
Oslo's geography is remarkable — within a few hours you can reach some of Norway's greatest mountain destinations. Two of the best mountain day trips from Oslo are Vettakollen (30 min, easy forest hike with city views) and Gaustatoppen (2.5 hrs, Norway's most spectacular viewpoint). Both are reachable as private guided day trips with hotel pickup and all driving included.

**What are the best mountains near Oslo?**
Two of the best mountains accessible as day trips from Oslo are Vettakollen (30 min, easy, 380m elevation, panoramic views over the city and Oslofjord) and Gaustatoppen (2.5 hrs, moderate, 1,883m, Norway's most spectacular viewpoint).

**Which mountain near Oslo is best for beginners?**
Vettakollen is the most accessible — an easy 3.5-hour forest hike just 30 minutes from the city centre. For those wanting a genuine summit experience without technical difficulty, Gaustatoppen is the best choice — a moderate 4–5 hour hike to one of Norway's greatest panoramas, 2.5 hours from Oslo.

**What is the closest mountain to Oslo?**
Vettakollen in Nordmarka is the closest mountain hike to central Oslo — just 30 minutes by car from the city centre, offering genuine forest and mountain terrain with panoramic views over Oslo and the Oslofjord.

**Can I do a mountain day trip from Oslo without a car?**
Yes. Oslo Hiking Tours offers private guided summer day trips to both mountains with hotel pickup from central Oslo and all driving included. No car hire, no navigation, no logistics required.

**How long do day trips from Oslo take?**
Vettakollen is a half-day — back before lunch. Gaustatoppen is a comfortable full day, returning by early evening.

**Does Oslo Hiking Tours offer anything besides day trips?**
Yes — Overnight in Nordmarka is a private guided overnight camping experience, separate from the mountain day trips. Guests hike into the forest in the late afternoon, the guide cooks dinner over a fire at sunset, and guests sleep in tents before hiking back out the next morning. All camping equipment is provided.

**Is there an overnight camping experience near Oslo?**
Yes. Oslo Hiking Tours offers Overnight in Nordmarka, a private guided forest camping trip just 30–45 minutes from central Oslo. It includes sunset, a fire-cooked dinner, sleeping under the stars, and a forest sunrise, with all equipment provided. It costs NOK 12,000 per group of up to 4 guests.
